method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery' (published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume)). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11752749). The ERS 2024 adult chylothorax consensus statement (Eur Respir J, DOI 10.1183/13993003.00470-2024) was preferred but the publisher page returned a bot challenge (HTTP 403), which was not bypassed. A BJS Open 2025 scoping review of chyle leak after pancreatic surgery was read and rejected because it covers incidence, not management.

claims.claim: CL is characterized by milky or white drainage fluid with triglyceride levels ≥ 110 mg/dL (1.2–1.4 mmol/L).
claims.source_text: CL is characterized by milky or white drainage fluid with triglyceride levels ≥ 110 mg/dL (1.2-1.4 mmol/L)
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Persistent leakage can lead to impaired wound healing, immunosuppression, malnutrition, extended hospitalization, and occasionally death; continuous CL significantly elevates mortality after surgery.
claims.source_text: Persistent leakage can lead to impaired wound healing, immunosuppression, malnutrition, extended hospitalization, and occasionally death … Continuous CL significantly elevates mortality rates in postoperative patients
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Chyle leak follows intraoperative lymphatic damage, a significant complication after lymph node dissection in cancer patients.
claims.source_text: Excessive trauma during vessel and tissue separation, incomplete ligation of injured lymphatic vessels, or inadequate heat application from the electrosurgical knife can cause intraoperative lymphatic vessel damage. This damage impedes lymphatic fluid reflux, leading to lymphatic leakage, known as chyle leaks (CL), a significant postoperative complication following lymph node dissection in cancer patients
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: NRS 2002 and PG-SGA are recommended for nutritional assessment; assess weight change, triceps skinfold thickness, mid-arm circumference and grip strength.
claims.source_text: NRS 2002 and PG-SGA are recommended for nutritional assessment in cancer patients (). Assessing nutritional status in CL patients involves evaluating changes in weight, triceps skinfold thickness, middle-arm circumference, and grip strength
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Monitor hepatorenal function, immunity and electrolytes during nutritional support, because chyle carries serum proteins, fat-soluble vitamins, minerals and immune cells.
claims.source_text: Chylous fluid contains serum proteins, fat-soluble vitamins, minerals, and immune cells. During nutritional support, monitoring hepatorenal function, immunity, and electrolytes in CL patients is essential to prevent severe electrolyte imbalances and immune system impairment due to chylous fluid leakage
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Many studies define a CL volume exceeding 1,000 mL within 24 h as high leak volume and < 1,000 mL as low leak volume; base dietary changes on chyle volume and check fluid balance daily.
claims.source_text: Dietary treatment modifications should be based on chylous volume. Although CL volume classification is debated, many studies define a CL volume exceeding 1,000 mL within 24 h as high leak volume and < 1,000 mL as low leak volume … daily monitoring of fluid balance is essential for CL patients
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Dietary therapy, as the most conservative treatment for CL, achieves full recovery in 66–100% of cases and is the preferred approach after surgery.
claims.source_text: Dietary therapy, as the most conservative treatment for CL, achieves full recovery in 66-100% of cases (). Its effectiveness and practicality make it the preferred approach for cancer patients diagnosed with CL post-surgery
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Form a multidisciplinary team (surgeons, nutritionists) to plan a personalised high-protein, low-fat diet, reviewed daily.
claims.source_text: Due to the complexities of CL management, forming MDTs is advised. Regular consultations with surgeons and nutritionists are essential to develop personalized dietary management plans tailored to the patient's condition, focusing on a high-protein, low-fat diet … healthcare professionals should evaluate and adjust the nutritional strategy daily
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: For those with low postoperative CL volume, a high-protein, low-fat diet is recommended, emphasizing fats from MCTs, maintained for 7–10 days.
claims.source_text: For those with low postoperative CL volume, a high-protein, low-fat diet is recommended, emphasizing fats from MCTs. This diet should be maintained for 7-10 days
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Dietary fat restriction should be maintained for 2–4 weeks post-resolution of CL to prevent recurrence.
claims.source_text: Dietary fat restriction, which reduces chyle volume and aids healing, should be maintained for 2-4 weeks post-resolution of CL to prevent recurrence
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: MCTs are absorbed directly into the portal vein, minimally affecting gut lymph production, which improves chyle colour and reduces drainage volume.
claims.source_text: Medium-chain fatty acids are absorbed directly into the portal vein through small intestinal cells, minimally affecting gastrointestinal lymph fluid production, thereby improving chyle color and decreasing the drainage fluid volume
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ MCT dose for adults: 50 to 100 mL daily, starting with 1 tablespoon 3–4 times daily and increasing gradually. Higher doses may cause steatorrhoea, mild GI discomfort and raised cholesterol in hyperlipidaemia.
claims.source_text: The typical daily dosage for adult ranges from 50 to 100 mL starting with 1 tablespoon taken 3-4 times daily. Higher doses may cause steatorrhea, mild gastrointestinal discomfort, and elevated serum cholesterol in patients with hyperlipidemia … Administration should be gradually increased
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: MCT can be taken orally as liquid or capsules, mixed into foods, sauces or cooking, or included in enteral feeds.
claims.source_text: MCT is well-tolerated and can be administered orally in liquid or capsule form. MCT oil can be incorporated into various foods, such as mixed with juice for salads and vegetables, added to sauces for fish, chicken, or lean meats, or used in cooking and baking. Additionally, MCT can be included in enteral feeding products.
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: If the patient cannot eat, give enteral feeding with MCT by nasogastric or gastrostomy tube until the leak resolves.
claims.source_text: For postoperative CL patients unable to consume food orally, enteral feeding with MCT via a nasogastric or gastrostomy tube should be initiated and continued until CL resolves
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ High leak volume: oral feeding can increase chyle, so start TPN promptly for complete bowel rest. TPN is also considered when a standard low-fat or MCT diet fails to reduce volume.
claims.source_text: Oral feeding can increase chylous volume, necessitating the prompt initiation of TPN to ensure complete bowel rest for patients with high leak volumes … For those unable to consume food orally post-surgery or with insufficient intake, and who do not achieve volume reduction despite a standardized low-fat or MCT diet, TPN may be considered
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: When TPN is used, limit its duration to 6–30 days because of catheter complications and cost; stop fasting treatment when CL volume falls below 50 mL.
claims.source_text: When TPN is utilized, its duration should be limited to 6-30 days to manage potential IV catheter-related complications and high costs … Fasting treatment should be discontinued if the CL volume falls below 50 mL
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Oral multivitamins are recommended on a fat-free or low-fat diet, with parenteral supplementation as necessary.
claims.source_text: A fat-free or low-fat diet can hinder the absorption of various vitamins, and the lack of regular parenteral micronutrient supplementation may result in wound dehiscence in CL patients. Therefore, oral multivitamins are recommended, with parenteral supplementation administered as necessary
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ If essential fatty acid deficiency risk is high, give a peripheral IV fat emulsion three times weekly at 250 mL of 20% solution per administration.
claims.source_text: In cases of high risk for essential fatty acid deficiency, a peripheral IV fat emulsion is recommended three times weekly at 250 mL of 20% solution per administration
claims.locator: Zhou et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 11:1478190, 'Best evidence summary for nutritional management of cancer patients with chyle leaks following surgery', published 8 January 2025 (2024 volume), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752749/, retrieved 2026-09-23
